questions.stem: A radio station broadcasts at a frequency of 100 MHz. If radio waves travel at 3 x 10^8 m/s, what is the wavelength of the broadcast?
questions.explanation: Using v = f x wavelength, rearranged to wavelength = v / f: wavelength = (3 x 10^8) / (100 x 10^6) = (3 x 10^8) / (1 x 10^8) = 3 m. A common error is forgetting to convert MHz to Hz (100 MHz = 100,000,000 Hz = 1 x 10^8 Hz), which would give an incorrect answer.

questions.stem: A sound wave in air has a wavelength of 0.5 m and travels at 340 m/s. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Using v = f x wavelength, rearranged to f = v / wavelength: f = 340 / 0.5 = 680 Hz. Option A (170) comes from multiplying speed by wavelength instead of dividing. Option C results from adding the values. Always rearrange carefully: dividing by 0.5 is the same as multiplying by 2.

questions.stem: A wave machine in a swimming pool produces waves with a frequency of 2 Hz and a wavelength of 1.5 m. How far will the wave travel in 10 seconds?
questions.explanation: First find speed: v = f x wavelength = 2 x 1.5 = 3 m/s. Then distance = speed x time = 3 x 10 = 30 m. Option A (3) only gives the speed, not the distance. Option B (15) comes from wavelength x time. Option C (20) comes from frequency x time. You need to combine the wave equation with the distance formula.

questions.stem: A student measures 8 complete waves in a ripple tank over a distance of 40 cm. The wave generator is set to 10 Hz. What is the speed of the waves?
questions.explanation: First find wavelength: 40 cm / 8 waves = 5 cm = 0.05 m. Then v = f x wavelength = 10 x 0.05 = 0.5 m/s. This is the same as 50 cm/s (option A), but since option C expresses it in standard SI units (m/s), both A and C are numerically correct in different units. However, 50 cm/s = 0.5 m/s, so both represent the same value. Option C uses SI units which is the standard. Option B confuses wavelength with speed.

questions.stem: When a wave passes from deep water into shallow water, its speed decreases but its frequency stays the same. What happens to the wavelength?
questions.explanation: From v = f x wavelength, if frequency stays constant and speed decreases, then wavelength must also decrease (wavelength = v / f). A smaller v with the same f gives a smaller wavelength. Option A is wrong because that would require speed to increase. Option B is wrong because wavelength depends on speed when frequency is fixed.
